concepts.definition: F15 describes release identification, publication, qualification, acceptance, selection and successor conservation. Its instance premises are recursive products, published point-in-time cuts available to uncontrolled consumers, movable shared carriers, source-matched derived assets, external services and predecessor-affecting successor lines. These premises are additional to the commitments. FOUNDATIONS owns the generic lineage taxonomy; this family traces and applies it without taking ownership.

grounding.quote: Its instance premises, which the commitments do not supply, are

concepts.label: Release and successor conservation family

concepts.definition: The lineage roles substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition are distinct identities with their own bases. A mutable workspace is not a fixed-identity product; an install acting as builder substrate is bound as a development product, without transferring meaning or authority to its authored product. A product definition is a source-project surface rather than the released artifact.

grounding.quote: substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition are distinct objects.

concepts.label: Distinct product lineage objects

concepts.definition: A stable repository-local key assigned by the Product release authority to one independently released source project.
concepts.label: Project Release Namespace

concepts.definition: The exact repository-relative source-project root and Git tree object selected for a cut. The root is a locator within the peeled commit rather than Product identity.

grounding.quote:
- Project Subtree: the exact repository-relative source-project root and
  Git tree object selected for one cut;

concepts.label: Project Subtree

concepts.definition: The mutable source-project state constructing a possible successor; its RC branch is a mutable project-qualified carrier for the current candidate window.
concepts.label: Candidate Source and RC branch

concepts.definition: An annotated project-qualified Git tag together with its exact Product release subject. It names a published candidate and, once accepted, a released Product; it realises the generic release cut.
concepts.label: Immutable RC Cut

concepts.definition: A mutable project-qualified tag alias naming the highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut for a project and version line. An optional, separately identified mutable release branch is a convenience carrier aligned to the selector's latest-published commit.

grounding.quote:
- Version-Line Selector: the mutable project-qualified tag alias naming
  the highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut for that project and
  version line; it realises the version-line selector of FOUNDATIONS §2;
  and
- Release Branch: an optional mutable project-qualified convenience
  carrier aligned to the same latest-published commit as the selector.

concepts.label: Version-Line Selector and optional release branch

concepts.definition: The declared exact Product member set or artifact, distinguished from its release-scoped claim surfaces and excluded co-located mutable source-project fields. Repository commits carry these sets without making all co-located files Product members.

grounding.quote:
- the exact Product member set or artifact constituting the release
  subject;
- the release-scoped claim surfaces describing that subject; and
- co-located mutable source-project fields excluded from both.

concepts.label: Product release subject

concepts.definition: Optional cut-carried surfaces include release notes, release and installed-distribution manifests, dependency declarations, package or installed-carrier metadata, qualification receipts, and branch and tag identity declarations.
concepts.label: Release-scoped assets

concepts.definition: The represented release process has three phases: mutable candidate construction; immutable RC publication with monotonic version-line advancement; and exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption. A published cut provides one exact subject for review, replay and possible acceptance.
concepts.label: Release process

concepts.definition: Qualification evaluates claims on an exact release subject, basis, observation boundaries and evidence, retaining owner verdicts, unresolved gaps and the complete successor relation.
concepts.label: Exact-cut qualification

concepts.definition: The human Product authority's acceptance of an exact immutable RC identity after applicable mandatory gates. This is distinct from publication, selector advancement and consumer adoption.

grounding.quote: - the human Product authority accepted the exact immutable RC identity.

concepts.label: Release acceptance

concepts.definition: An explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs, verifies and pins an immutable RC. Its externally presented read-only Adoption Plan binds the current definition bytes and basis to the exact target cut, tag object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest and emits a deterministic plan digest.

grounding.quote:
Adoption is a separate
explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs,
verifies and pins the selected immutable RC.

the Adoption Plan of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4, binds the current Product
Definition bytes and basis to the target immutable cut, annotated tag
object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest, then emits a
deterministic plan digest.

concepts.label: Consumer adoption and Adoption Plan

conditions: A Product authority declares the relation because one corpus and its required distributed or derived assets need to remain usable as one versioned set.
concepts.definition: An explicit cross-Product relation naming every required Product and asset, exact source dependency, owning authorities, qualification boundary and publication transaction. Co-location, equal versions and a common actor do not establish it.

grounding.quote:
The declaring
relation names every required Product and asset, the exact source
dependency, its owning authorities, the qualification boundary and the
publication transaction. Path co-location, equal version text or a common
actor cannot infer the relation

concepts.label: Release-Matched Asset Cohort

concepts.definition: A successor's claim about one affecting predecessor claim: conserved means retained; superseded means replaced by an accepted successor relation; intentionally removed means removed by current Product authority; not applicable means no successor effect with a bounded reason. These are claim predicates, not evaluation result values or the decision owner's acceptance disposition. An unresolved disposition states no claim and has no result.

grounding.quote:
An unresolved disposition states no claim and so has no result: in the
qualification of the affected claim it is a planned assessment without a
closed result

concepts.label: Successor semantic disposition

concepts.definition: A provenance table recording claimed conservation of rc.2 RELEASE_METHOD.md rows and their current loci. The table records restatement and changes of expression, not evaluated conservation or new rule authority. Generic release objects are defined in FOUNDATIONS and realised here.

grounding.quote:
Every conserved row is restated in this member's own
text; a route is provenance only.

concepts.label: RELEASE source-disposition record

concepts.definition: Tier-2 owner of the particular spec-driven method: position and identity, constitutional chain, manifesto and litmus tests, requirement/design/trace/live-surface law, outcome conservation, change management and classification, consistency and sprint boundaries, ambiguity and lifecycle, lineage, migration, procedures, design records and build-tenant binding. It is realised from FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION; its clauses are not foundational. PRODUCT_DEFINITION owns project binding, ASSURANCE testing law, TICKETS work carriers and RELEASE release mechanics.

grounding.quote:
nothing here is foundational, every clause
names the principle that requires it (P0 to P6, FOUNDATIONS §3), and each
mechanism could be realised differently under the same principles.

concepts.label: SPEC_METHOD

concepts.definition: The meta-constitutional process for relating goals, intent, product, requirements, design, realisation, evidence and repricing, including sufficiency, requirement truth and authority flow. It aims to make software re-derivable, auditable and correctable under explicit authority. With surviving domain specification it should support rebuilding a project process after implementation loss.

grounding.quote:
the method should still be sufficient to bootstrap a new
spec-driven project process from scratch; the method plus the surviving domain specification
can reconstruct the project

Its point is to make software
re-derivable, auditable and correctable under explicit authority.

concepts.label: Process constitution

conditions: Under the selected complete basis.
concepts.definition: The bounded context urn:stdo:bounded-context:method-identity names STDO's four areas: Specification owned by SPEC_METHOD; Ticketing by TICKETS; Design by DESIGN_MODULE; and the complete Outcome-Driven Development area by ODD. This expansion neither makes those members independently selectable nor reduces the released Product to four members.

grounding.quote:
The expansion does not make the four owning
members independently selectable and does not reduce the released product
to four members: consumer authority remains one complete immutable released
cut with its exact member inventory

concepts.label: STDO method identity

concepts.definition: The bounded work-wave surface naming current overriding concerns; more immediate than intent and higher-level than product definition and requirements. Temporary focus stays here until intentionally repriced into deeper layers.

grounding.quote:
The goals surface is the bounded work-wave surface: it captures the current
overriding concerns for the next body of work, keeps temporary focus out of
deeper constitutional layers until it is intentionally repriced there, and
is more immediate than intent while remaining higher-level than product
definition and requirements.

concepts.label: Goals

concepts.definition: The surface of purpose, domain direction, and directional change that is in or out of scope.

grounding.quote:
Intent states why the
system exists and what directional change is in or out of scope;

concepts.label: Intent

concepts.definition: The mutable source project's current, present-tense product definition, key terms, boundaries and end-state shape, bridging direction to decomposable obligations. It is neither an immutable release cut nor an installed product. Its layout-neutral routing overlay locates actual authorities and tenant realisations without becoming rival constitutional truth.

grounding.quote:
It is not the immutable release cut
and not the installed product; those are the lineage objects of FOUNDATIONS
§2

the definition is a routing
overlay, not a rival truth surface

concepts.label: Product Definition

concepts.definition: The full constitutional WHAT: invariant truths, capabilities, constraints, guarantees, governance and verification obligations that the project must make true, with explicit acceptance criteria and enough information for downstream design derivation.

grounding.quote:
Requirements are the constitutional what of the project. They are not
limited to user-visible features: the live requirement surface may include
capabilities, invariants, constraints, governance and verification
obligations; what matters is that each requirement states something the
project must make true.

concepts.label: Requirements

concepts.definition: The structural HOW: decisions, interfaces, topology, file placement, carrier documents, entry/control surfaces, runtime wiring and lawful tenant boundaries realising requirement truth. ADRs are durable design records, not a separate constitutional layer or requirement surface.

grounding.quote:
Design
defines the structural decisions, interfaces, carrier surfaces and delivery
topology that make those truths achievable; ADRs are one durable form of
design record, not a second constitutional layer above design.

concepts.label: Design and design records

concepts.definition: Realisation performs design decisions as code in software, human procedure in a human process, or both in a mixed environment. The tenant binding selects the carrier; the responsibilities called Code, Events and Projection do not themselves require a codebase or event store.

grounding.quote:
Code
realises those decisions where the selected execution environment is
software; a performed human procedure realises them where it is a human
process, and both where it is mixed (§11).

concepts.label: Code or other bound realisation

concepts.definition: The owned homeostatic chain is Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis → Repricing at the change-class layer. Events retain what happened in a selected stream, ledger, signed record or observation log; projection reconstructs current truth when that record suffices, without necessarily replaying a complete stream; delta reveals intended/realised drift; scenarios test operational meaning; gap analysis exposes insufficiency; repricing updates the appropriate layer.

grounding.quote:
Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code
  → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis
  → Repricing at the layer its change class names

concepts.label: Constitutional chain and homeostatic loop

concepts.definition: Two independent requirement axes: category identifies Capability, Constraint / Guarantee, Governance or Verification truth; lifecycle status identifies Active, Deferred, Superseded or Orphaned standing. Capability supplies behaviour/function/surface; Constraint / Guarantee bounds behaviour through invariants or laws; Governance controls lifecycle, authority, visibility, release or operator action; Verification concerns tests, evidence, traceability, qualification or forensics.

grounding.quote:
| Capability | a behaviour, function or surface the system must provide | what can the system do |
| Constraint / Guarantee | an invariant, law, safety property, portability rule or semantic guarantee that bounds how the system may behave | what must always remain true |
| Governance | a policy or control rule over lifecycle, authority, visibility, release or operator action | what governs use and change |
| Verification | a requirement on tests, evidence, traceability, qualification or forensic surfaces | how do we know the claim is true |

concepts.label: Requirement category and lifecycle classification

concepts.definition: For every material product, application, module, function, runtime/plugin/public-interface/data surface or capability, the canonical lifecycle is intent, requirement, build, assurance, release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry and retirement. Each phase is answered, explicitly not applicable with a reason, or unknown with a named gap; these are declared states, not evaluation results.

grounding.quote:
Any material
product, application, module, function, runtime surface, plugin
surface, public interface, data surface or capability has an operational
lifecycle, whose canonical chain is intent, requirement, build, assurance,
release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry, retirement.

concepts.label: Operational lifecycle and phase states

concepts.definition: A product-outcome-bearing work wave selects one unresolved, directly verifiable, product-defined outcome and its acceptance interval. Evidence classes are material advance (accepted movement and the only product progress), bounded prerequisite readiness, preservation/repeated proof, and regression. Prerequisites and decision-discriminating experiments are separately admitted bounded growth bases.

grounding.quote:
Every product-outcome-bearing work wave identifies one explicitly selected,
unresolved, directly verifiable product-defined outcome and declares the
acceptance interval for that instance.

concepts.label: Selected outcome and admitted growth bases

concepts.definition: A tenant's declared requirements calculus, computational calculus and execution environment. It identifies operations, outcomes mapped into the core, and resource measures with units and boundaries. Construction steps, data meaning and execution remain separate accounts; mappings between accounts are transformations with preservation obligations.

grounding.quote: the division of a binding into requirements calculus, computational calculus and execution environment

concepts.label: Build-tenant binding

concepts.definition: F10 describes how specification governs realisations, assuming owned layers, layered interpretable surfaces, several changing realisations and immutable releases. It traces laws, domain choices and owners separately. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step-produced facts; P5 derived from P0/P6 with an open-world premise.

grounding.quote:
Standing of the commitments cited (FOUNDATIONS §3): P0
recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and
P2, with P0's premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable; P5
derived from P0 and P6, with P0's open-world premise.

concepts.label: Chain, outcome and build-tenant family

grounding.quote: an operation's outcome is not its acceptance

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Release process is separate from live specification and owns neither Product meaning nor consumer adoption. Release handling follows intake triage; an open release window authorises no untriaged change. Refused, stopped or fail-closed operations, invalid states and failed checks report in the core and none means success. Family-table consumers apply only what the owning section decides; open-question and source-disposition sections decide nothing. The source marks P3/P6/P1 independent, P0 recovered, P5 derived from P0/P6 under the open-world premise, and P4b derived from P0/P2 under non-reacquirability; additional domain choices are not promoted to derived law.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced core algebra and full commitment definitions are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
Equal version text does not collapse these identities. Branches and the
version-line selector may move. An immutable RC tag never moves (P3).

constraints.statement: All seven release-publication identities remain distinct despite equal version text. Candidate source, release cut, release subject and selector also remain distinct generic objects. Mutable branches/selectors may move; immutable RC tags never move. A selector supplies discovery rather than exact identity or governing basis, and shared carriage supplies no membership.

conditions: For a continuing release line; qualified ref shapes apply to future publication in a shared release source.
exceptions: The explicitly declared single-project unqualified profile and preserved historical refs have the separate conditions retained below.
Alternative spelling requires the collision-freedom policy retained in naming_variation.

grounding.quote:
`<project>` is one explicit Project Release Namespace. It matches
`[a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*`, contains no slash, is unique within the
release source, and remains stable for the continuing release line.

RC branch:              refs/heads/rc/<project>/<version>
immutable RC cut tag:   refs/tags/<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>
version-line selector:  refs/tags/<project>/v<version>
release branch:         refs/heads/release/<project>/<version>

constraints.statement: The Product release authority assigns a namespace matching [a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*, without slash, unique in the release source and stable along its continuing line. Directory/display/definition/package names and matching versions cannot infer or reassign it. Shared-source future publications use the four exact grounded ref shapes, with short tags <project>/v<version>-rc.<n> and <project>/v<version>, never unqualified future cut/selector refs. The Specification Stack allocations specification_methodology, axiom_indexer and stdo_representation distinguish refs without merging Products or implying dependency/composition.

conditions: For an immutable cut in a shared release source.
exceptions: The repository-root locator is spelled . alone; its subtree tree equals the repository-root tree.
constraints.statement: The cut binds every item in the grounded seven-part inventory. The subtree root is a slash-separated Git path with no leading/trailing slash, empty component, . component or .. component; each non-root component names exact tree-entry bytes at the peeled commit. Moving the project changes locator and cut identity without reassigning namespace. A monorepo tag does not admit sibling subtrees; unrelated siblings remain carrier state. Inventory or payload digest without qualified ref, commit, subtree root and subtree tree is not a complete reacquirable release identity.

conditions: When adopting project qualification or resolving historical/public cut coordinates.

grounding.quote:
Project qualification is prospective. Existing unqualified refs retain
their names, objects, peels and public links.

constraints.statement: Existing unqualified refs retain names, objects, peels and public links; a historical tag cannot be recreated, re-annotated, moved or replaced, even if an archival ref also reaches it. Product-local cut names and stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/ remain unchanged; qualified Git transport identity is not inserted into the logical URI. Resolution binds the logical cut to its exact historical or qualified ref and fails closed if one project-local coordinate names different tag objects. On a version line spanning transition, latest is the greatest positive ordinal across preserved historical and qualified future cuts. The first qualified publication creates the qualified selector; the historical selector stays at its existing object, ceases to be current and is not force-moved to imitate the namespace.

grounding.quote: There is no second final cut after an accepted RC.

constraints.statement: Publication immediately exposes the new highest ordinal through the selector. Acceptance remains a verdict over that exact RC and produces no second final cut or carrier. Any byte change capable of affecting the Product or a release-scoped claim requires publication and review of a higher immutable RC.

conditions: During candidate construction and before RC publication.

grounding.quote:
The intended Product boundary, release-scoped claims, excluded
source-project state and qualification basis become explicit before RC
publication. A material scope change is repriced instead of being silently
absorbed

constraints.statement: Mutable source is explicitly non-operative for released consumers. Before publication, make Product boundary, release-scoped claims, excluded source state and qualification basis explicit. Reprice material scope changes rather than silently absorbing them.

conditions: When publishing an RC; shared-source tag creation uses qualified names.
exceptions: The general publication push is atomic where transport supports it; the coordinated-cohort rule separately requires atomic support or refusal.
The release branch is optional.

grounding.quote:
10. records enough ref, subtree, identity and inventory evidence to
    reacquire the cut without trusting a mutable checkout.

constraints.statement: In source order: confirm triaged scope and lawful constitutional re-entry; declare exact Product subject and claim set; reconcile release-facing assets; run proportionate pre-RC qualification and operator checks; commit exact carrier; record namespace, subtree root and tree; create annotated immutable cut and annotated selector over that commit; push carrier, RC branch, cut, selector and any release branch atomically where supported; remotely verify cut, selector and any release branch at the highest published RC commit; retain reacquisition evidence. Further work increments n on the same line when it remains applicable; bounded review repair alone does not require a minor-version increment. A higher published RC without matching selector advancement is invalid and fail-closed, never permission to resolve the older cut as latest.

exceptions: Artifact presence can prove usability only when presence itself is the exact claim.

grounding.quote:
Evidence matches the claim. Source success does not prove packaged or
installed behaviour; packaging equivalence does not prove semantic
behaviour; artifact presence does not prove usability unless presence is
the exact claim

constraints.statement: Qualification binds namespace, qualified immutable ref, annotated tag object, peeled commit, repository tree, subtree root/tree, declared members, exact claim bytes, governing Product/release basis, every claimed property and observation boundary, evidence subjects, owner verdicts, unresolved gaps and complete predecessor/successor relation. Source success, packaging equivalence and mere artifact presence cannot substitute for stronger claims. Acceptance requires completed required exact-cut review/operator checks and human acceptance of that subject. A qualifying-byte change leaves the verdict on the old RC and requires a higher one; acceptance never moves or rewrites the selector or creates a final carrier.

conditions: For advancement within one project version line.
exceptions: Release-branch alignment applies when that optional carrier is used.
The general transport push is atomic where supported.

grounding.quote:
Advancement is refused when the target has no matching immutable annotated
RC tag, any higher ordinal already exists, the selector would move to a
lower RC, or the selector and release branch would not align to the same
highest commit

constraints.statement: Identify the exact new annotated immutable tag, ordinal and peel; confirm no higher ordinal exists and the selector is absent or at a lower ordinal on the same project line; atomically create/force-update the annotated qualified selector to the highest commit; align any release branch; push the full carrier/RC/cut/selector/optional-branch set atomically where supported; remotely verify selector peel and matching immutable annotated tag. Refuse each grounded refusal condition. Movement is strictly monotonic by ordinal: later defects require higher cuts, never old-tag movement or selector rollback. The selector means v<version>-rc.latest while every concrete RC stays addressable.

conditions: For channel resolution and adoption.
exceptions: Intentional older-cut retention explicitly names its immutable URI and digest and uses exact-basis operations such as sync.

grounding.quote:
Channel adoption also refuses a same-line target whose ordinal
is below the Product Definition's current exact basis.

constraints.statement: The selector answers which highest published cut exists, never which cut governs a consumer. The operative basis is the exact release URI plus installed-manifest digest; selector movement updates no consumer. Resolution requires an annotated selector with distinct peeled commit; missing peeled ref fails closed rather than being read as a lightweight tag. Enumerate the selected namespace's published cuts, including preserved historical cuts during transition; choose the greatest positive ordinal; require both cut and selector to be annotated and peel to the same commit. Lag or other target fails closed. Channel adoption refuses a lower same-line ordinal than the current exact basis. Older-cut retention is not expressed through a latest channel.

conditions: Before mutating any Product Definition through adoption.

grounding.quote:
Planning inside a mutating invocation is not
external presentation and cannot authorise itself.

constraints.statement: Read-only presentation and mutation are separate invocations. Mutation requires the exact presented deterministic plan digest as operator acceptance and re-derives it before changing definitions. Selector, target, manifest or definition drift invalidates acceptance. Fleet adoption uses one aggregate digest over all exact per-definition plans. Planning inside mutation cannot self-authorise. The hashing rule and command boundaries belong to PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4.
constraints.uncertainty: The full hashing algorithm and manager command boundaries are not supplied.

conditions: For every release-scoped surface used by a cut.

grounding.quote:
Before RC publication, each used surface is reconciled to the exact RC
subject. After publication, changing one of those bytes creates a
different candidate and therefore requires a higher RC tag.

constraints.statement: Reconcile each used asset to the exact subject before publication; any subsequent change to those bytes requires a higher RC. The selector has no content-reconciliation phase because it adds no Product bytes. Exact version/RC identity belongs in release-scoped carriers and consumer basis bindings; live constitutional version labels follow the specification surface rule.

conditions: Before qualification and after publication, respectively.

grounding.quote:
Once the immutable RC is published, no post-review
carrier delta is admitted into that cut.

constraints.statement: Before qualification declare namespace and exact subtree root, exact subject members/artifact, describing claim surfaces and mutable source fields excluded from both. Exact subtree tree and inventory distinguish subject from carrier; co-location supplies no membership. Published cuts admit no post-review carrier delta. Publication-caused ticket/source bookkeeping occurs afterward on the continuing source branch and cannot move the immutable tag.

conditions: For a declared cohort; the five-member population applies to a release-matched STDO stack.
exceptions: Independent qualification is required where applicable; a stale index may remain immutable history.

grounding.quote:
Qualification normalises only that leading cut-name marker
and requires exact suffix equality.

The cohort is incomplete when a required member is missing, stale,
differently versioned, built from another source cut, or unable to
reproduce its declared source-member and digest closure.

constraints.statement: Every required member uses exactly <version>-rc.<n>, rendered with v for cut names/refs and without v in asset fields; qualification removes only that leading marker. Equality establishes matching only, never merged identities, inventories, tags, judgments or authorities. The closed STDO cohort contains the exact standards cut; its distributed spec plugin/host assets; exact Axiom Indexer mechanics Product; exact STDO Representation Product; and its released a_c.STDO program/map or equivalent index with complete source-member inventory, individual digests, member-set digest and derivation cut identity. Any grounded incompleteness condition makes it incomplete. A covered source-member change invalidates the old derived candidate for the successor; regenerate, mechanically validate, independently qualify where required, and release the index under the same new cut name. A stale historical index cannot accompany changed source as current cohort.

conditions: For coordinated STDO cohort construction and publication.
exceptions: Release branches remain optional.

grounding.quote:
Exact installed-manifest identity includes the annotated STDO tag object,
so a same-commit carrier containing both that identity and derived child
bytes would be self-referential.

constraints.statement: Avoid tag/manifest/child self-reference through this order: commit A freezes corpus, plugin, release record and qualification bytes; create the annotated STDO cut locally without pushing; install and verify that exact cut to produce every derivative's manifest identity; derive/freeze Axiom Indexer, STDO Representation, index and cohort record in commit B; qualify B against the local STDO tag before child tags; prepare annotated child tags and Product-local RC branches/selectors/optional release branches; run a mandatory post-tag pre-push qualification over all annotated objects/peels, selectors, branches, normalised version mappings, target commits and the exact closed ref set, fetching/binding every destination's expected object or required absence; atomically publish only that qualified carrier branch and complete Product ref set in one transaction.

conditions: For cohort publication and remote verification.

grounding.quote:
If the remote does not support atomic ref publication, publication
refuses. The process has no sequential-push fallback.

constraints.statement: Refuse without atomic remote support. Every immutable tag is create-only with bound remote absence; every mutable carrier, RC branch, selector and release branch uses an explicit per-ref compare-and-swap lease in the same transaction. A missing expected ref, unexpected tag or changed remote object stops publication; refetch and repeat complete content and local-ref-graph qualification before another push. Lease mismatch permits no unguarded force, partial push or in-place expectation update. Remote verification fails closed for any required absent/lightweight/differently versioned ref, wrong Product commit or misaligned selector/release branch. Later bookkeeping cannot move immutable tags.
constraints.uncertainty: The source's lightweight-ref wording occurs within a mixed tag/branch ref set; its exact applicability to branches is not explained.

conditions: For normal cohort qualification and any separately authorised recovery.
exceptions: A historical same-version backfill is possible only under separately authorised recovery law naming that exception.

grounding.quote:
Post-publication qualification verifies the same relation from remote refs
and refuses a partial cohort

constraints.statement: Content qualification binds commit-A tag/manifest, commit-B tree, all target refs/version markers/member inventories/index bytes and complete source digest closure, establishing taggability without a qualifying-byte change. After ref creation, local-ref-graph qualification binds annotated objects, peels, targets, exact push set and every remote expectation/absence to unchanged qualified content. Remote qualification verifies that same relation and refuses partial cohorts. Recovery still binds the historical cut and same name and requires remote completeness; it cannot move historical tags, add subject bytes or claim original-publication atomicity. Normal successors use atomic publication. Added/changed cohort law governs only a higher RC containing its bytes, never retroactively creates an earlier cohort.
constraints.uncertainty: The separately authorised recovery law is not supplied.

exceptions: Independent exact-cut review is required where applicable.
Release-blocking gaps may be addressed by explicit narrowing of claimed scope.

grounding.quote: Each criterion is a mandatory gate

constraints.statement: An RC may be accepted only with pre-RC qualification passed for the subject; independent exact-cut review passed where required; required operator review complete; stable intended scope and successor relation; accurate exact-cut assets; all release-blocking gaps, including promotion-blocking findings, closed or scope explicitly narrowed; and human Product authority acceptance of the exact immutable identity. These gates apply regardless of post-change check selection; retained evidence satisfies them only under FOUNDATIONS validity conditions. Acceptance attaches to the cut and neither advances nor rolls back the selector; adoption separately evaluates the presented latest exact target and mutates only after plan-digest acceptance.
constraints.uncertainty: The full retained-evidence validity conditions and finding-based promotion rules are externally referenced.

conditions: A release claim depends on an external backend, transport or operator-facing service.

grounding.quote:
A clean skip caused by an unhealthy external dependency is an evaluation
not performed, which has no result

constraints.statement: A dependency can remain outside Product for carrier/migration classification while blocking its dependent claim. A clean skip due to unhealthy dependency is Not performed, has no result and establishes no capability pass, even if Product classification remains correct. Qualify against a healthy dependency or narrow the claim before acceptance.

conditions: For every predecessor claim capable of affecting a successor.

grounding.quote:
an obligation stays obligatory, a preference
stays a preference, and every permitted exception and scope condition
survives, or the claim is not conserved.

constraints.statement: Identify one exact predecessor RC whose origin remains immutable for the candidate, and assign one semantic disposition to every affecting claim. Retain/reassess evidence; an earlier conserved reading applies later only if owning text and consumer bindings are unchanged or change is shown irrelevant. Unresolved disposition blocks the affected claim's qualification. Compare the same material case, scope and authority, must/may/prohibited outcomes, absent triggers/exceptions/premises, owning text and consumer bindings, with counterexamples exposing changed decisions. Patch absence need not mean loss; names/code similarity and whole-package equivalence assertions do not prove conservation. Indicative wording may bind; rewriting must/shall alone proves neither conservation nor supersession. Preserve obligations, preferences, every permitted exception and scope condition. Conserved records predating this test must be reevaluated before qualification and remain unresolved meanwhile. Evaluate each disposition predicate into its own core result; a recorded disposition alone establishes nothing and is never itself a result.

conditions: A maintenance or support line may affect retained claims.

grounding.quote:
Where a maintenance or support line may affect retained claims, the
release basis identifies the watched source, observation boundary,
inclusion policy and successor candidate. Relevant changes receive
semantic disposition at material integration and exact-cut qualification.
The consumer owns its record, branch strategy, comparison and proof
mechanism

constraints.statement: The release basis names watched source, observation boundary, inclusion policy and successor candidate. Relevant changes receive evidence-based semantic dispositions at both material integration and exact-cut qualification. Record, branch strategy, comparison and proof mechanism are consumer-owned. EVALUATION §5 applies this section's disposition record to acceptance and is a separate owner.

grounding.quote:
"must remain usable as one versioned set" is written "need to
remain usable", the condition of declaration and not a new obligation;

it
decides nothing beyond the rules it names.

constraints.statement: The table claims conservation of the listed rc.2 release-context, position, identity, ref, subtree/history, phases/publication/qualification/advancement/adoption, naming/assets/subject/cohort/recovery, acceptance/external-dependency, successor and open-question rows at their recorded loci. Its generalisations remove bold emphasis, replace method references with §9/member references, use British spelling and treat need to remain usable as a declaration condition, not a new obligation. It records the family table and Results paragraph as new, and dispositions-as-claims/unresolved-as-no-result as new interpretation; clean skip applies existing Results law. The family table adds no rule beyond its named owners and distinguishes derived consequences from added choices. The tenant frontier is cited as the corpus's predecessor-disposition record, not supplied proof.
constraints.uncertainty: The predecessor document, missing §1 body and tenant frontier are not supplied; the table's conservation claims are not independently established.

grounding.quote:
Routes are
provenance only; nothing here depends on that cut to be applied.

Constitutional examples use neutral capability and authority identities:
they demonstrate enabled capabilities rather than cite a consumer as
precedent, whose particulars cannot become method law

constraints.statement: Specification is constitutional source, not retrospective commentary. The system should primarily declare truths, structures, interfaces, constraints and evidence surfaces and let lawful processing derive work; imperative procedure remains subordinate to declared authority. Constitutional examples use neutral identities, not consumer particulars as precedent. rc.2 #anchor routes point to the published v2.5.1-rc.2 SPEC_METHOD, and rc.2 MEMBER routes to that cut's named member; these are provenance only, not application dependencies.

grounding.quote:
The authoritative split is strict: the surfaces bound as WHAT define WHAT;
design and realisation surfaces define HOW; no build tenant, design, code,
definition overlay or derived surface becomes co-equal constitutional
authority with the bound WHAT

constraints.statement: The method defines process constitution; goals name current concerns, intent domain direction, product definition current mutable-project meaning, requirements derived live obligations, and shared/tenant design concrete mechanisms. Product Definition binds actual authority locations and tenant-registry realisations under one shared specification. Conventional GOALS.md, INTENT.md, PRODUCT.md and specification/requirements/ names require no existing project to move or duplicate files. WHAT-bound surfaces retain strict constitutional authority over HOW, tenants, code, overlays and derived surfaces; folder placement is not constitutional.

exceptions: Blocking/escalation follows declared risk appetite except for hard-stop prerequisite failures.
Scenarios supply end-to-end proof where capability claims require it.

grounding.quote:
detection is mandatory; blocking or escalation is
policy under declared risk appetite, except for hard-stop prerequisite
failures

constraints.statement: Every method-governed product publishes a layout-neutral definition locating constitution, local constitutional decisions, collective frame bases, WHAT, independent tenant HOW, work surfaces and explicit composition. Material terms resolve only under context identity, owner, selected basis and governed scope; equal spelling grants no meaning/authority, explicit imports/translations/equivalences/disambiguations govern seams, and zero or multiple applicable meanings fail closed. Major boundaries reduce lawful interpretations and explicitly surface major ambiguity; detection is mandatory. Implementations never substitute for constitutional documents. Iteration is cumulative repricing; new intent comes from real-use gap analysis. Every live requirement family has design ownership, classification and closure or deferment; every design record is requirement-grounded; shipping behaviour traces to authority. Sprints price proof and force close review but supply no authority and cannot hide drift. The canonical statement owns no additional law beyond its cited sections.
constraints.uncertainty: Full semantic-resolution, ambiguity-policy and sprint rules reside outside the supplied text.

exceptions: Negative proof is required where drift is plausible.
Mapping recorded in a_c additionally follows AC-013.

grounding.quote: A mapping from one account to another is a transformation, so it states and discharges its preservation

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: F10 consumers inherit no decisions beyond owners. Realisation-claim closure evidence includes authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof where drift is plausible and remaining open pressure; closure/evidence law remains with TICKETS/EVALUATION/ASSURANCE. Each lineage object keeps its identity and a consumer selects one complete released version; reusable method changes retain one authority relation from evidence to the realising consumer. Different means/executors neither accept nor reject a realisation; human performance is not adjudication, structural validity is not correct execution, convenient stacks weaken no obligation, and only the obligation's owner can weaken WHAT. Bindings identify operations, core-mapped outcomes and finite-evaluable resources/units/boundaries. Calculi serve where their declared laws hold regardless of executor. Tenant design owns calculi/environment/resources; project law owns multi-tenant development. Separate construction accounts and discharge mapping preservation under refinement and, when recorded in a_c, AC-013. The Intent owning this corpus owns the three-account choice. §8 applies ACTIVATION rather than supplying new foundational law; §12 only records dispositions.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed external closure, refinement, resource and adoption-chain mechanisms are not supplied.

exceptions: A path may be prescribed in requirements when the path itself is constitutional.
Projection requires retained-record sufficiency, not necessarily complete event-stream replay.

grounding.quote: Every link is load-bearing.

constraints.statement: Every chain link is owned: missing downstream repricing, unowned requirements, ungrounded design or code without design creates accidental law. Carrier responsibilities apply in each selected execution environment without imposing unselected software/event stores. Product Definition stays present-tense mutable-project meaning, distinct from cut/install. Requirements may require delivery/control surfaces; design chooses where/how unless placement itself is constitutional. Gap-driven constitutional repricing re-enters the change-class layer and creates goals/intent when work wave, direction or scope changes.
constraints.uncertainty: The detailed change-class-to-layer mapping is not supplied.

exceptions: Transitional paths may stay live when explicitly retained as compatibility features.

grounding.quote:
It treats derived artifacts,
indexes, trace matrices, reports, automation and generated views, as read
models, never as constitutional truth. If these claims do not hold, the
work is not spec-driven.

constraints.statement: Define current goals before deeper repricing, intent before implementation, explicit present-tense product definition before detailed requirements, and full constitutional WHAT rather than a feature list. Prefer declarations over imperative prescriptions. Design explicitly bridges requirements to derivable code; each major gate reduces lawful interpretations before downstream realisation. Claims require evidence through scenarios, tests, events, projection and delta. Constitutional gaps trigger specification change; iteration preserves directional authority. Once new current reality is established, erase transitional live-product paths except explicitly retained compatibility features. Derived artifacts/indexes/matrices/reports/automation/views are read models, never constitutional truth. Failure of these commitments means work is not spec-driven.

conditions: Any one listed failure is sufficient for the source's not-spec-driven conclusion.

grounding.quote: The work is not spec-driven if any of these holds

constraints.statement: The thirteen failures are: inability of a competent team to derive conformant intent from goals, Product Definition from intent, requirements from product, design from requirements, or code from requirements plus design; a live requirement missing status, category or design owner; a live requirement lacking downstream realisation or explicit deferment; code behaviour without requirement/design authority; rewriting a live constitutional domain artifact in place; a capability claim without operational evidence; drift located by intake triage in constitutional source without repricing that source; major boundary ambiguity neither recorded nor explicitly governed; or a material product/module/function/application/runtime surface/capability lacking both declared lifecycle signal and a recorded gap for unanswered release, deployment, live-use, telemetry or retirement questions.
constraints.uncertainty: This is the source's criterion, not a judgment of any supplied project.

requirements and different codebases the same design.

constraints.statement: Spec-driven layers must be reconstructable in chain order by a competent actor; this is sufficiency, not deterministic uniqueness. Boundary failure is an upper-layer defect: goals may be unclear/contradictory/not orienting; intent vague/contradictory/not concrete; product underspecified/contradictory/not decomposable; requirements underspecified/contradictory/polluted by accidental implementation; design incomplete/ambiguous/not operational for code. ADRs and design documents are load-bearing. Ambiguity governance and EVALUATION layered-sufficiency law apply; design-profile coverage/change/reuse rules keep their own ownership.
constraints.uncertainty: Full external conformance and design-profile gate details are not supplied.

a gap becomes

Constitutional gaps re-enter their change-class layer and flow forward through that class's affected layers; new goals/intent arise when work wave, direction or scope changes. New intent requires concrete repeated real-use pressure and explicit analysis, not abstract speculation or ad hoc coding. Iteration cumulatively refines requirements/design, re-derives code and feeds implementation/testing/replay/scenario gaps into repricing while preserving the full authority direction.

Before a downstream specification artifact is treated as complete, the

Write live constitutional truth in present tense; delete, supersede or move dead law to commentary, including during migration. Use current truth and affected boundary, never version branding merely for recency. Before completeness, check the whole affected span for clear change class, lawful re-entry, downstream derivability and agreement among active intent/product/requirements/design/qualification. Otherwise the consistency gate stays open.

constraints.statement: Classify every live family by both Status and Category in header metadata; neither may be missing and nothing live remains unclassified. Superseded transfers ownership and requires Implements and Supersedes on the governing design record. Active needs a written/updated owning design decision. Orphaned is removed or explicitly superseded. These statuses/categories/legacy classes, evidence classes, migration old-path/inherited/implementation classes, ADR statuses and change classes are declared states, never core results. Active/material advance is not satisfied; Deferred/Orphaned is not falsified. Evaluations produce their own predicate-bound core values. Shipping code/tests trace to live requirement and design authority; hidden ungoverned Product behaviour is prohibited even if functional. Unowned requirements, ungrounded design, undocumented deferment and ownerless behaviour are drift. Tests of implementation habit lock in drift. Persistent event/projection delta triggers intake diagnosis among code, requirement/design stack, predictive model and observation. Capability without scenario has unverified operational meaning. Feature-labelling guarantees/governance/verification misclassifies them; in-place constitutional correction corrupts history. An unexpressible real-use gap re-enters Requirements or upstream at its change-class layer, not through a code hack.

Live domain artifacts, once published as live

from the live surface.

constraints.statement: Multiple live surfaces may accumulate as versioned constitutional history, never scratch space. Incorrect live artifacts are superseded, withdrawn or deleted from the live surface, not silently mutated. Superseded transitional paths/scaffolds/fallbacks retire and have no permanent authority; retained responsibility satisfies the migration closure relation. Preserve past through version control, operational event history where present and superseded artifacts. Compatibility shims need not ship forever.

constraints.statement: Product Definition and requirements supply enough constitutional signal for downstream lifecycle derivation or explicitly record ambiguity, without specifying every mechanism. Every phase is answered, inapplicable with reason, or a named Gap:/Unanswered:. This is ambiguity detection, not a requirement that each requirement become a release plan. Missing signal cannot be supplied by local convention, implementation precedent, prompt prose or fixtures: reprice the constitutional owner or carry explicit governed debt. Phase states map to no core value; answered/inapplicable cannot substitute for satisfied, and evaluations return independent predicate-bound results.

exceptions: An assurance capability explicitly defined as Product behaviour may count as product progress; its evidence still does not author the claim.

grounding.quote:
Acceptance exhausts only that instance and its
declared acceptance interval; it does not discharge an enduring guarantee,
a recurring obligation or a broader product family beyond the accepted
instance.

constraints.statement: Judge progress and supported-path promotion against the same selected outcome and acceptance interval. Only accepted material advance projects progress; bounded prerequisite work names the enabled obligation, preservation/repeated proof is useful but not progress, and regression adds no progress. Owner acceptance ends that instance's selection of further progress work; witnesses remain preservation/regression evidence. Further work is preservation, another admitted outcome's named bounded prerequisite, or a new lawfully repriced change, never extra progress on the accepted instance. Selecting another existing unresolved outcome is goals/sequencing; changing meaning/scope or introducing an outcome re-enters Product. Evidence-surface completion cannot select/enlarge/replace outcomes. An artifact's Product-output and evidence roles must be separately declared.

conditions: For material realisation growth within a product-outcome-bearing wave.
exceptions: Admission or renewal may be performed by an explicitly bounded proxy of the owning work-wave authority.

grounding.quote:
Ended authority cannot be renewed by repair,
continuation, evidence, active ticket or run state, or prior admission;
further material work requires a new admission by the owning authority or
its explicitly bounded proxy

constraints.statement: Growth requires the selected unresolved outcome, an admitted named bounded prerequisite, or an admitted named bounded experiment whose stated observation discriminates a stated decision for that outcome. A prerequisite/experiment grants only its provisional bound, not enlarged outcome, downstream work, promotion, closure or waived design/safety/authority/release law, including applicable design-profile prime law. Record owner/proxy admission in durable goals/ticket authority with bound and exhaustion/falsification condition. A decision-discriminating observation exhausts its experiment. Ticket/contract drafting or validation, active status and prior admission cannot create/extend/renew authority. Outcome acceptance, prerequisite discharge, experiment decision resolution, any admitted terminal condition, rejection, withdrawal, supersession, repricing-away or evidence falsification ends the basis. Further material work needs new admission.

exceptions: Independent parallel work may proceed under its own admitted basis.
Affected-path promotion may resume after repair, repricing or owner acceptance.

grounding.quote:
A regression or unresolved gap blocks further promotion on the affected
path until repaired, repriced or accepted by the owning authority.

constraints.statement: Retention as supported behaviour, evidence, regression protection or bounded donor material grants no growth authority. Consumers own deletion/archive/quarantine/salvage mechanics; salvage carries only explicitly re-adopted semantics, not enclosing authority, dependencies, completion or work-selection power. Regression or unresolved gap blocks only its affected promotion path until repaired, repriced or owner-accepted; independent admitted work is not globally serialised and cannot be counted as this outcome's progress. Outcome success is necessary delivery evidence, not complete Product/release closure.
